hypothesis: A paired task-text audit may expose evidence-supported supplementary PF concerns in historically high-rated tasks, without assuming their original rubric scores were wrong.
null_result: No same-task agreed concerns, or concerns predominantly unknown/disputed, is a valid result. Additional properties do not retroactively invalidate Rahimi ratings.

sampling.V2: Six tasks: two uniform seeded draws from each attempt-number tertile
sampling.V3: Six tasks: two uniform seeded draws from each attempt-number tertile
sampling.PIPELINE: Twelve ready tasks: four seeded draws per attempt tertile; availability-conditioned controls

claim_policy: Only same-property two-judge agreement with exact source quotes counts as an agreed task-evidence concern. Mathematics concerns remain unresolved for interpretation review. Original anchor tensions are computational review candidates, not proof a high rating is false. No student or learning claims.
calibration_policy: One frozen instrument; no prompt tuning to achieve perfect controls or reject direct tasks. Record misclassifications and disagreement. Proceed if runtime/schema permits paired assessment, preserving unknowns. Genuine runtime or parser repairs require new version provenance.

task.title: Markers
task.body: Share 24 markers equally among 6 students. A table and a bar drawing show the same six groups.
task.question: Use only 24 divided by 6. Write the result and show it in a table or drawing. Do not choose another method.

task.title: Consistency
task.body: Team A scores 1, 3, 7, 9. Team B scores 1, 5, 5, 9. Both sets have mean 5 and range 8.
task.question: Decide what more consistent should mean here. Invent or choose a criterion, compare the teams with it, and defend why that criterion is useful. No particular spread formula is prescribed.

controls.learning_target: Develop a measure of consistency beyond the mean and range.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Compute a mean and largest-minus-smallest range.

task.title: Paint shares
task.body: Five friends share 3 liters of paint equally. Partial liters are allowed; paint can be poured freely.
task.question: Find a way to determine each share, represent your reasoning, and explain why the shares are equal and exhaust the paint.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Partition a whole into equal parts and add fractions.

task.title: Mixtures
task.body: Strip A records 2 blue cups and 3 white cups. Strip B records 4 blue cups and 6 white cups. These are the supplied mixtures to compare.
task.question: Decide whether they have the same concentration and explain how your comparison works.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Compare the amount of one substance per unit of another.

task.title: Garden discovery
task.body: For a fixed perimeter of 24 meters, a square has the greatest rectangular area. Two example gardens measure 2 by 10 meters and 6 by 6 meters.
task.question: Explain why the square wins and draw a graph showing that conclusion.

controls.learning_target: Discover which rectangular garden maximizes area for a fixed perimeter.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Multiply side lengths and add boundary lengths.

task.title: Point total
task.body: A player scores 2 points and then 3 points. The record states that the total from these two scores is 6 points.
task.question: Use this record to explain the total.

task.title: Discounts
task.body: A jacket costs 80 dollars. Shop A discounts it by 20 percent and Shop B discounts it by 15 dollars.
task.question: Decide which price is lower and explain.

task.title: Pump records
task.body: A pump uses 15 liters in 5 minutes, 30 liters in 10 minutes, and 45 liters in 15 minutes.
task.question: Check whether there is one constant liters-per-minute rate. You may divide for unit rates or multiply to test equivalent ratios, and display that same check in a table, graph, or equation.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Calculate one quantity per unit of another.

task.title: Runner
task.body: Runner A covers 6 kilometers in 30 minutes. Runner B covers 9 kilometers in 60 minutes.
task.question: Which runner was faster? Develop and explain a comparison that would also work for different distances and times.

controls.learning_target: Compare rates for unequal distances and times.

task.title: Best garden
task.body: You have 24 meters of fencing for a rectangle. Side lengths must be positive whole numbers of meters.
task.question: Which design gives the greatest growing area? Choose how to search, develop an argument that you have not missed a better design, and decide what evidence would convince another group.

controls.learning_target: Discover area maximization under fixed perimeter.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Find rectangle area and perimeter and enumerate whole-number possibilities.

task.title: Travel
task.body: A bus travels 120 kilometers, but its travel time is not provided. Students cannot collect further data and must give one exact numerical speed.
task.question: What exact speed in kilometers per hour did the bus travel? Do not make any assumptions.

controls.learning_target: Determine speed from distance and time.

task.title: Class trip
task.body: There are 18 students, including 6 who need wheelchair-accessible seats. A small bus costs 90 dollars and has 8 seats including 2 accessible seats. A large bus costs 150 dollars and has 12 seats including 4 accessible seats.
task.question: Choose a combination of buses for everyone. Decide how to weigh cost against unused seats, make your recommendation, and explain the tradeoffs. You may start by listing combinations.

controls.learning_target: Model competing constraints and make a justified decision.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Add, multiply and compare totals in a table.

task.title: Floor tiles
task.body: A floor is a rectangle 4 meters long and 7 meters wide.
task.question: Use only length times width to calculate its area. Show that same multiplication in a grid drawing, table, and equation. Do not choose a different calculation.

task.title: Fair lunch choice
task.body: Meal A costs 6 dollars, has 400 calories, and supplies 15 grams of protein. Meal B costs 8 dollars, has 600 calories, and supplies 20 grams of protein.
task.question: Define what good value should mean for these meals, choose or invent a numerical comparison, and explain who might reasonably choose differently. No value formula is given.

controls.learning_target: Construct and critique a numerical measure from several quantities.

assumed_prior_knowledge.taught_as: Divide quantities and combine rational-number values.
